title: A cohomology class of a torsion sheaf comes from a constructible sheaf
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and $i:Z\to X$ a morphism of schemes with $Z$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-pc-scheme] (the cases used are $Z=X$, $i=\mathrm{id}_X$, and $i$ a closed immersion). Write $i^{-1}:\Ab(X_{\Et})\to\Ab(Z_{\Et})$ for the inverse image of abelian sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], $H^q(Z_{\Et},-)$ for etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and, for a morphism $\varphi$ of abelian sheaves on $Z_{\Et}$, $H^q(\varphi)$ for the induced map of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]; for a sheaf of modules, $i^{-1}$ and $H^q$ are taken of its underlying abelian sheaf. Let $q\ge0$.
(1) (Torsion abelian sheaves.) Let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] and $\xi\in H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}F)$. Then there are an integer $n\ge1$, a sheaf $G$ of $(\mathbf Z/n)_X$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] which is constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] (with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n$; so $G$ is a torsion constructible abelian sheaf: finite stalks, killed by $n$), a morphism $u:G\to F$ of abelian sheaves, and a class $\zeta\in H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}G)$ with $H^q(i^{-1}u)(\zeta)=\xi$.
(2) (Sheaves of modules over a finite ring.) Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ and $\xi\in H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}F)$. Then there are a constructible sheaf $G$ of $\Lambda_X$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], a morphism $u:G\to F$ of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules and a class $\zeta\in H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}G)$ with $H^q(i^{-1}u)(\zeta)=\xi$.
(For $Z=X$, $i=\mathrm{id}_X$, identified with the identity functor, this says that $\xi\in H^q(X_{\Et},F)$ lies in the image of $H^q(X_{\Et},G)\to H^q(X_{\Et},F)$. The map $u$ cannot in general be taken to be a monomorphism, i.e. $G$ cannot be taken to be a constructible subsheaf of $F$, when $X$ is not Noetherian: see the split report.)

source.place: Lemma 09ZE (lemma-efface-cohomology-on-closed-by-finite-cover), line 14901, proof, first sentence: 'By Lemmas 03SA (lemma-torsion-colimit-constructible) and 03Q5 (lemma-colimit) we can find a map G -> F with G a constructible abelian sheaf and xi coming from an element zeta of H^q(Z, G|_Z)'; replaces the imported blueprint statement (blueprint file sk-thm-p1/lemma-weil-pbc-constructible-approximation.md, order 1126)

proof.text: For part (2), use the natural comparison of module inverse image and abelian inverse image. Apply its cohomology natural isomorphism to send ξ to a class in the underlying abelian sheaf of i⁻¹_Mod F. The constructible restriction class theorem supplies G, its constructibility witness, a:G→F and a stage class z with H^q(U(i⁻¹_Mod a))(z) equal to that transported class.

The constructible restriction theorem records a finite locally closed stratification and finite-value trivializations on its strata. Use the same strata as Scheme.Stratification and apply finite_locally_constant_module_values_iff on each stratum. This proves the source-library IsConstructibleSheaf predicate used by Gabber, without changing the meaning of constructibility.

Whisker the inverse-image natural isomorphism with Sheaf.functorH in degree q. Naturality at a gives H^q(i⁻¹_Ab U(a))(e_G(z)) = e_F(H^q(U(i⁻¹_Mod a))(z)). Substitute the equality for z and cancel e_F with its inverse. Thus the class e_G(z) maps to ξ. This proves part (2) and is the complete proof of exists_isConstructibleSheaf_hom_of_henselianRing in Gabber. Parts (1) below remain the natural-language torsion-abelian argument; the existing Lean declaration represents only part (2).

*Part (1): $F$ is the filtered union of the $F[n]$, and $\xi$ comes from some $F[n]$.* $F$ is torsion, so by definition [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] the subsheaves $F[n]=\ker(n:F\to F)$, indexed by the positive integers ordered by divisibility (a directed set), with the inclusions $j_n:F[n]\hookrightarrow F$, form a colimit cocone $(F,(j_n))$ in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ ($c_F$ is an isomorphism). As in step 2, $i^{-1}$ preserves colimits [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits], so $(i^{-1}F,(i^{-1}j_n))$ is a colimit cocone of the directed system $i^{-1}F[n]$, and [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit] on the quasi-compact and quasi-separated $Z$ makes $\varinjlim_nH^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}F[n])\to H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}F)$, induced by the $H^q(i^{-1}j_n)$, bijective. Every element of a directed colimit of abelian groups has a representative at some stage [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups]; so there are $n\ge1$ and $\xi_n\in H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}F[n])$ with $H^q(i^{-1}j_n)(\xi_n)=\xi$.

source.place: Lemma 03SA (lemma-torsion-colimit-constructible), line 12216, part (3) and the proof of part (2): 'First write F = union F[n] ... view F[n] as a sheaf of Z/nZ-modules and apply (3)'

proof.text: *Part (1): apply part (2) with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n$.* The abelian sheaf $F[n]$ is killed by $n$, so it carries a (unique) structure of sheaf of $(\mathbf Z/n)_X$-modules extending its abelian structure [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-killed-by-n-zmod-modules] (2), and its underlying abelian sheaf is $F[n]$. Part (2) (steps 1-3), applied to $X$, $i$, the finite ring $\mathbf Z/n$, this module sheaf and $\xi_n$, gives a constructible sheaf $G$ of $(\mathbf Z/n)_X$-modules, a $(\mathbf Z/n)_X$-linear map $u':G\to F[n]$ and $\zeta\in H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}G)$ with $H^q(i^{-1}u')(\zeta)=\xi_n$. Put $u=j_n\circ u':G\to F$, a morphism of abelian sheaves. Then $H^q(i^{-1}u)(\zeta)=H^q(i^{-1}j_n)(H^q(i^{-1}u')(\zeta))=H^q(i^{-1}j_n)(\xi_n)=\xi$: $i^{-1}$ is a functor [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and $H^q$ is functorial in the sheaf, since if $\tilde\varphi,\tilde\psi$ are lifts of $\varphi,\psi$ to K-injective resolutions then $\tilde\psi\circ\tilde\varphi$ lifts $\psi\circ\varphi$, and $H^q(-)$ does not depend on the lift [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]. This proves (1). (Stacks applies 03SA(2), whose proof is exactly the passage $F=\bigcup_nF[n]$ followed by 03SA(3); taking the two colimits one after the other avoids assembling one index category, as in [lem-weil-pbc-curve-constructible-reduction] step 5.)

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For a torsion sheaf $F$ on an affine henselian pair and a fixed class
$c\in H^q(T_0,F_0)$, there is a quasi-compact etale neighbourhood $U\to T$
and a constructible sheaf $C$ on $U$ with a monomorphism $C\hookrightarrow F|_U$
through which a cocycle representing $c$ factors.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Choose a split etale hypercover $U_\bullet\to T_0$ whose $(q+1)$-skeleton is
finite and quasi-compact and a cocycle $c\in\Gamma(U_q,F_0)$. Write its
finite components as $U_{r,a}$ for $0\leq r\leq q+1$ and denote all face and
degeneracy maps by $\partial^i_{r,a}$ and $s^i_{r,a}$. Choose quasi-compact
etale lifts $\widetilde U_{r,a}\to U\to T$ and sections of $F$ representing
the finitely many sections in $c$ and in the equations $dc=0$.

Enlarge the finite list by applying every $\partial^i_{r,a}$ and
$s^i_{r,a}$ to every chosen section. The simplicial identities are now a
finite list of equalities on finite fibre products. Shrink the lifts once so
that all equalities hold on the closed fibre and all maps factor through one
quasi-compact etale neighbourhood $U\to T$. On each lifted component let
$C_{r,a}$ be the subsheaf of $F|_U$ generated by this finite list. The
equalizer loci of pairs of generators give a finite stratification on which
$C_{r,a}$ is locally constant with finite fibres, hence constructible.

Closure under all displayed face and degeneracy maps gives a simplicial
constructible subsheaf $C_\bullet\subseteq F|_{U_\bullet}$. The cocycle lies
in $\Gamma(U_q,C_q)$ and the equation $dc=0$ remains true in $C_\bullet$.
Take the image of the augmentation $C_0\to F|_U$ and its finite iterated
extensions through degree $q+1$, then sheafify; this gives a constructible
subsheaf $C\hookrightarrow F|_U$ through which $c$ factors. Monicity is
checked at a geometric stalk: a finite combination of the generators maps to
zero in $F$ precisely when it is already zero in the generated subsheaf.
Thus every face map, cocycle, and equality used by the selected class is
contained in $C$.

split_report.summary: Statement rewritten from the vague imported one ('a cocycle factors, after a quasi-compact etale neighbourhood, through a monomorphism C -> F with C constructible torsion') to the form Stacks uses in the proof of 09ZE (efface-cohomology-on-closed-by-finite-cover, the lemma behind Gabber's theorem 09ZH-area): for qcqs X, a morphism i:Z->X with Z qcqs (Z=X or a closed subscheme), a torsion abelian F and xi in H^q(Z,i^{-1}F), there are n, a constructible Z/n-module sheaf G, a map u:G->F and zeta with H^q(i^{-1}u)(zeta)=xi; part (2) the same for sheaves of modules over a finite ring Lambda (the form the h1 user proves inline in its steps 2-3). The morphism i is included because 09ZE needs the class on the closed subscheme Z. The monomorphism of the imported statement (and of the brief's 'constructible subsheaf C of F') was dropped: it is false for non-Noetherian X. Counterexample: X=Spec(prod_N F_2) (a Stone space; every point closed; constructible subsets are clopen), x a non-principal ultrafilter point (closed, not open), F=x_* Z/2 (pushforward along the closed immersion of x), q=0, Z=X, xi=1 in H^0(X,F)=Z/2. H^0 of a subsheaf C -> F is injective, so xi in the image forces the section 1 into C(X); the stalks of F are Z/2 at x and 0 elsewhere, all generated by 1, so C=F. But F is not constructible: the stratum T containing x would be clopen, F|_T finite locally constant, so its support {x} would be open in T, hence in X. Stacks 09ZE itself only takes a map G -> F (the pushout F' = G' + _G F is mono since G -> G' is), so nothing downstream needs the mono; on Noetherian X images of constructible sheaves are constructible and the mono form holds. The imported proof (cocycle on a split hypercover, generated subsheaf) was replaced by the Stacks route: 03SA(3) (lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaf-colimit-constructible), forgetful and i^{-1} commute with colimits, 03Q5 (lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit) on qcqs Z, an element of a filtered colimit comes from a stage (elementary), and for (1) F = colim F[n] by the definition of torsion, then (2) with Lambda=Z/n. No new nodes. stmt_deps: removed lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stage-killing (not a statement dependency; the old statement only pointed at its hypotheses) and def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes (replaced by def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf).
